protocolProfile.recordMarker: Every new custody, release authorization and release ACK requires protocol=ltds-processing-spool-v2, schemaVersion=2, and its *_v2 receiptType.
protocolProfile.compatibility: This is not the existing Viewer v1 source-release ACK. Preserve v1 unchanged. The v1 endpoint/verifier must reject this protocol, schema version and receipt type; the v2 endpoint/verifier must reject v1 records. No fallback, downgrade or cross-profile replay is allowed.
protocolProfile.resultAcceptance: Result acceptance remains on the separately specified existing Reference v2 contract; it is not wrapped in this spool profile. Use its closed schemaVersion=2 PartialAcceptance (receiptType=partial_result_acceptance) and AcceptedCopyAck (receiptType=accepted_copy_ack) records, with no added protocol field, and its exact LTDS-PARTIAL-ACCEPTANCE-V2� canonical acceptance digest. The resultAcceptanceIssuer role comes from authenticated transport configuration. The candidate does not assign or implement that endpoint route; it must not be silently treated as /api/v2/processing-spool.

sourceRootConstraint: The configured processing-spool is a subfolder of the existing Model-Viewer ZFS dataset. A whole-dataset snapshot is not a subfolder-only pin or capacity reservation. No dataset, snapshot, path, ACL, endpoint, key or service is created by this proposal.

authentication.mode: mutually authenticated service transport with an externally configured principal-to-role map
authentication.bodyIssuerRule: issuerId is only a label; it must equal the authenticated peer principal resolved to the expected role. A body field, self-digest, SQLite row, bearer supplied by a caller, or local lock is not authentication.

roles.resultAcceptanceIssuer: authorized Viewer/NAS accepted-copy service; never a worker
roles.sourceReleaseAuthorizer: authorized Viewer retention authority; never a worker or processing coordinator
roles.sourceStorageExecutor: independently configured storage service with exclusive spool-root ownership and writer/deletion fencing

hashDomains.canonicalMetadata: UTF-8 JSON, ASCII lexicographic keys, array order preserved, no whitespace, booleans distinct from integers, nonnegative safe integer fields, valid scalar Unicode

resultAcceptance.wireProfile: Reference v2 contract only: schemaVersion=2, exact receiptType markers partial_result_acceptance and accepted_copy_ack, closed schemas from contracts/reference-v2-candidate/contract.schema.json, and no ltds-processing-spool-v2 protocol field. Do not downgrade to the colliding Viewer source-release v1 ACK profile.
resultAcceptance.acceptanceDigest: AcceptedCopyAck.acceptanceSha256 = SHA256(ASCII(LTDS-PARTIAL-ACCEPTANCE-V2) || 0x00 || canonicalUTF8(complete PartialAcceptance record)); no fields omitted. Canonical metadata rules come from the Reference v2 contract.
resultAcceptance.verification: The issuer must verify the received bytes, exact size and digest, required product closure, and exclusive accepted-copy custody before committing PartialAcceptance. AcceptedCopyAck echoes the exact operation, receipt, canonical acceptance digest, binding, result-set identity, manifest digest, accepted artifact IDs in order, and storage receipt ID.
resultAcceptance.replay: Idempotency is keyed by authenticated issuer principal plus ackOperationId. Exact canonical request replay returns the original byte-identical receipt/ack. Reusing the operation ID with any changed identity, payload, inventory or digest conflicts. Unknown response or missing receipt leaves worker and scheduler holds in place.
resultAcceptance.cleanup: AcceptedCopyAck proves only the authenticated issuer's recorded acceptance. It does not authorize source-input deletion, producer-output deletion, heavy-slot release, publication, or job terminalization by itself. The coordinator must persist the exact ack in its durable outbox/acceptance journal before changing its own state.

spoolCustodyReceipt.objects: Exact ASCII-objectId-ordered inventory of physical spool-copy identities: objectId, physicalObjectId, objectGeneration, byteSize, sha256 and custodyReceiptId. physicalObjectId is an opaque service-owned handle resolved beneath the verified spool root to a contained opened file identity; it is never a caller path.
spoolCustodyReceipt.authority: A trusted storage executor returns this only after independently resolving the exact attempt and re-reading every opened source byte under a fenced writer/purge boundary. The external principal must map to sourceStorageExecutor; the receipt and hashes alone are not custody.
spoolCustodyReceipt.capacity: capacityReservationReceiptId must resolve to an independently checked reservation with sufficient remaining space for source copies, concurrent result transfer/expansion and any retained result copy. A logical counter, statvfs sample, field named reservedBytes, or a snapshot of the parent Model-Viewer dataset alone is not a physical reservation.
spoolCustodyReceipt.retention: No time-based deletion. Objects remain held until an explicit sourceReleaseAuthorization and durable sourceReleaseAck both reconcile.

sourceReleaseAuthorization.objects: Exact ordered immutable inventory from the authenticated spool custody receipt. Each object binds objectId, physicalObjectId, objectGeneration, byteSize, sha256 and per-object custodyReceiptId.
sourceReleaseAuthorization.authority: Only the configured Viewer retention-authority principal may issue this record after it independently confirms the exact attempt is terminal, no retry or downstream stage can read the spool copy, delivery is resolved or explicitly not required, and the configured retention policy permits release. The authorization is limited to the exact processing-spool copy; it never names the Viewer source dataset, permanent raw Emlid CSVs, or accepted result copies.
sourceReleaseAuthorization.freshness: For a new release operation, authorization must be unexpired and bound to the current spool-root generation, custody receipt, terminal receipt and policy revision. An exact already-committed operation may be queried/replayed after expiry solely to recover its prior outcome. Expiry, stale generation, unknown terminal state, policy rollback, unknown ACK or uncertain writer state means retain/hold.
sourceReleaseAuthorization.effect: Authorization permits the storage executor to reconcile and delete only the exact listed spool-copy objects after it independently verifies the writer fence and file identities. It does not authorize deleting original Viewer inputs or results.

sourceReleaseAck.deletedObjects: Exact inventory from the authorization, each paired with a unique durable filesystem deletion receipt ID that resolves to the operation's immutable per-object journal. The executor records the full intent before unlink, verifies file identity/size/hash and no active writer under its independent fence, unlinks only listed objects, synchronizes affected directories, then commits the immutable ACK. Partial or uncertain effects stay in that durable journal and remain held; missing paths alone never prove deletion success. Reconcile the exact old journal and old-generation custody after restart. After expiry, do not perform new destructive effects with the expired authorization; any remaining or uncertain objects require operator-reviewed recovery and a fresh custody receipt that accounts for the old journal before a new authorization. Never silently discard old-generation objects.
sourceReleaseAck.replay: Idempotency is keyed by authenticated storage-executor principal plus operationId. Exact replay returns the immutable prior ACK; changed authorization or inventory conflicts. No second deletion pass is inferred from a missing file.
sourceReleaseAck.expiry: For a new operation, current time, every per-object unlink effect and required directory synchronization, and durable ACK commit must be strictly earlier than authorization expiresAt. At the exact expiry instant the authorization is expired. Check trusted time before each irreversible step and again after each effect/sync; require a bounded operation-time budget before starting. If any operation can cross the deadline or its completion time is uncertain, persist outcome_unknown and hold; do not issue a success ACK. After expiry, only read-only replay of a byte-identical ACK already committed in the authenticated durable operation ledger is permitted.
sourceReleaseAck.crashRecovery: Persist exact operation intent and per-object state before unlink; persist each observed unlink and directory-sync effect before advancing. After crash, first reconcile the exact old operation journal and old-generation custody under the writer fence. Never infer deletion from an absent path or create a receipt for an unobserved effect. Keep every extant or uncertain object held under its original identity. After authorization expiry, no new destructive effect may use that authorization. Any remaining objects require operator-reviewed recovery and a fresh custody receipt that explicitly accounts for the old-generation journal and every retained/uncertain object before a new authorization; rotating the spool generation alone never drops old custody.
sourceReleaseAck.scope: This ACK reports deletion of the processing-spool copy only. It is not a ZFS snapshot deletion, result acceptance, producer cleanup receipt, Viewer source deletion, or permission to purge original client data.

globalInvariants: All record schemas are closed; identities and all five job binding fields compare exactly.
Accepted artifact IDs, result manifest digest, source object inventory, source closure digest and storage receipt identities are exact, immutable and non-empty where required.
Receipt IDs, physical object IDs, per-object custody receipts, deletion receipt IDs and operation IDs are unique within their issuer/hold scope.
A stale worker, worker self-claim, untrusted issuer string, timeout, lost ACK, missing receipt, DB rollback/restore or ambiguous process state cannot release data or capacity.
Only an independently authenticated storage executor with actual file writer fencing may perform the authorized unlink; candidate validation does not establish that implementation or authority.
No TTL, status label, completion callback, accepted-copy ACK or SQLite flock substitutes for explicit release authorization plus durable storage ACK.

releaseVector.expected: synthetic binding pass only; this vector does not prove signatures, mTLS, NAS custody, capacity, writer fences, filesystem durability, or deletion
